description:
FILED s470bl (Opus, 2026-09-05) while shipping #1022 half (b).  LOUD, not
silent: the exit site dies with perl's own `Can't "last" outside a loop block`.

    sub f { next }
    my $n = 0;
    for my $i (1..3) { $n++; f(); $n += 100 } continue { $n += 1000 }
      perl:  n=3003     (3 iterations, each running the continue block)
      PCL:   Can't "next" outside a loop block

    sub f { last }
    my $n = 0;
    { $n++; f(); $n += 100 } continue { $n += 1000 }
      perl:  n=1
      PCL:   Can't "last" outside a loop block

WHY.  The frame (%p-loop-driver) re-enters the iteration tagbody at the point
the corresponding LEXICAL exit would have reached, and for `next` that is the
POST-BODY forms.  A foreach's continue block is not there: it lives INSIDE the
per-iteration binding, because it reads the loop variable.  A bare block's
sits after the tagbody, inside the block the wrapper cannot re-enter.  So
Parser2 declines `:dyn` for both (`@dyn = () if @cont` in the foreach branch;
`!defined $cont` in the bare-block branch) and the macros treat the
combination as a compiler self-inconsistency and die (rule 12).

`while`/`until` are NOT affected -- their continue block IS a post-body form,
so a caught `next` runs it (probed: n=3003, matching perl).

THE FIX SHAPE, if a row ever needs it: emit the continue form TWICE for a
licensed foreach -- once inside the per-iteration binding (today's position)
and once as a post-form with its own re-read binding `(let ((var (elt-fn vec
(1- i)))) CONT)`.  Costs nothing at run time (the second copy is only reached
after a throw) and doubles the continue block's compiled size.  Not done here
because no row in perl-tests, perl's own t/ or the CPAN board has the
combination -- measure before writing it.

docs/not-supported.md names this under the dynamic-loop-exit section.

=== DONE (s473e, Opus, 2026-09-08) ===
SHIPPED.  A `continue` block no longer declines the frame.

THE FIX SHAPE THE TASK SKETCHED (emit the continue twice, once in the binding
and once as a post-form with a re-read binding) IS WRONG, and a probe caught it
before it shipped: re-reading the element gives the continue block the value in
the vector, not the value the body left.  `for my $i (1..3) { $i = 99 } continue
{ push @c, $i }` is 99 99 99 in perl; the re-read design reads 1 2 3, and so
does a value copied at binding time -- where the compiler proved the loop
variable unboxable, a body write is an ordinary `setf` of the LET binding.

WHAT SHIPPED: on a FRAMED loop the continue block becomes a per-iteration
CLOSURE, created inside the binding and CALLED from %p-loop-driver's post-forms
(`%p-foreach-continue-thunk`, one helper for both foreach expanders).  A closure
over the binding sees assignments to it, so raw and boxed loop variables are
both right, and there is exactly ONE copy of the continue form.  A bare block
hands its continue to `p-dyn-once`, which gained the driver's RESUME variable:
a caught `next` ends the loop-once only AFTER running the continue (perl
n=1001), a caught `last` skips it (n=1), a caught `redo` restarts without it.
The bare block's licence scan now covers the continue block too, since a sub
called there can exit the loop (probed).

Compiler side: `@dyn = () if @cont` and `!defined $cont` are gone;
`_has_continue_block` was already dead and described the removed rule, deleted.

MEASURED: 11 probes vs perl 5.40.3 all match (redo, a `last` performed BY the
continue block, nested labelled loops, the foreach alias writing through).
corpus-diff vs 92d2eb74 IDENTICAL across 111 files -- no framed continue'd loop
exists in the corpus, which is why nothing moved.  Guard `Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t`
section 9 (10 rows; 8 fail on a 92d2eb74 extraction, 2 are the negatives).
ir-conform 186-loops-exits + 187-loops-exits left known-fail.tsv.
docs/ir-spec.md 6.2 and docs/not-supported.md updated.
subject: A `continue` block on a `foreach` or a bare block DECLINES the #1022(b) dynamic-exit frame, so a dynamic `next`/`last` into such a loop dies instead of running it
